message: PH-4.2 says no dates appear, but preserving every lifecycle affordance retains existing plan-age, verify/work, saved-plan, and quickfix-closure dates; confirm that the no-dates boundary applies to the new Overview only.

notes: Correct catch, and the answer is: the no-dates boundary applies to the NEW Overview only. The spec's Boundaries list ('No dates, estimates, burndown or velocity') constrains what the HIERARCHY presentation adds — it is not a mandate to strip timestamps the lifecycle board already shows. PH-4.2's own criterion requires the lifecycle board to remain 'with every current affordance intact', so removing plan-age, verify/work, saved-plan or quickfix-closure dates would violate that criterion AND be scope creep beyond this story. Build the Overview with no dates; change nothing about existing lifecycle timestamps.

message: PH-4.2 requires no dates anywhere, but preserving every lifecycle affordance conflicts with existing saved/worked/closed dates and building-age markers in factory/board/index.html; clarify whether the prohibition applies only to Overview.

notes: Same question as S-0001, and the fault is the contract rather than your reading of it — two workers found it independently. PH-4.2's acceptance criterion is now AMENDED to say it explicitly: no dates in the OVERVIEW; the lifecycle board's existing plan-age, verify/work, saved-plan and quickfix-closure timestamps stay exactly as they are. Re-read the amended brief.

message: PH-4.4 requires './forge board --repo factory/board/example' to serve a minimal example, but make_server currently reads HTML from <repo>/factory/board/index.html; fixing the server requires factory/scripts/forge_cli/board.py outside write scope, while copying or symlinking the board into the example is not authorized by the minimal tree criterion.

notes: Correct, and the flaw is mine — the criterion asserted --repo would serve a data-only tree without checking that board.py:535 reads the page from the --repo TARGET. Ruling: the board PAGE is machinery paired with board.py, so resolve index.html from the RUNNING CODE (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / 'board' / 'index.html'), not from the data root. In an ordinary repo the running code is the vendored copy, so behavior is unchanged there; a data-only --repo directory then works. board.py is now IN your write scope and a new criterion covers it, including a test that a repo whose index.html differs from the harness's still serves the running code's page. Re-read the amended brief.
